segments.t: Joining me now, Jean Munster, managing partner of Deepwater Asset Management.
Jean, happy Friday.
Great to have you back.
Fantastic to be back.
So, Jean, it's been a tough few months to be a tech investor.
The NASDAQ is down 9% in November alone, 18% off the highs.
Is the AI trade over?
You know, the early read here is that it's broken down
and I've had conversations with other investors that, in fact, this is over.
We've had now this bursting of the bubble.
We will know if it's over probably in two months.
This is something that it's not going to, we won't have a rebound next week
that's going to tell us that, in fact, this was just a head fake
or if it even steps down lower, if it means that it's over at that point.
So we can have further declines and it not being over.
And so my sense is that the market is making a prediction right now
that there's about a 75% chance that the broader AI trade,
and I would define that as invest in AI companies
and getting outsized returns over the next year.
The, I think, three quarters of the market believes we're probably at the end.
I'm in a different place.
I think that there has been several unique kind of pieces that have led us here.
And those pieces really don't have good analogues from the past
that we could go back and look at when things had ended.
And I want to stress that we're never going to get a perfect lineup
of something that happens currently and say, you know, this, for example,
we had this three companies go out of business and run going out of business
or whatever it might have been.
And therefore, it's a perfect match versus what's going on today.
Typically, it rhymes and what we're seeing now, there is no rhyme to it.
